title: PlanningRoundTriggered
description:
An allocation round has been opened for one satellite over one horizon bucket. This event is the audit record of a scheduling decision boundary — it says what was on the table before anything was decided, which is what makes a committed plan reviewable rather than merely observable.

ROUND IDENTITY is (satellite_id, bucket_start). That pair is the Postgres advisory-lock key, so allocation for a given satellite-bucket is single-writer while different satellites plan fully in parallel. The lock granularity matches the invariant granularity — the non-overlap constraint is per-satellite, so the lock is per-satellite. That is the whole trick, and it is why serialising the planner does not create a global throughput ceiling.

TRIGGER is separate from identity. A bucket can be planned more than once: once on the cadence timer, and again when new opportunities arrive for a bucket already planned. That is what makes plan supersession a first-class concept rather than an edge case (see supersedes_plan_id here and on planning.plan.committed.v1).

correlation_id.description: A round aggregates many requests, so it cannot inherit a single request's correlation_id. It gets a fresh one; the per-request threads are re-joined through candidate_request_ids and through the request_id on each unfulfilment event.

causation_id.description: For OPPORTUNITY_DEBOUNCE triggers, the event_id of the opportunities event that tipped the threshold. Null for CADENCE.

bucket.description: Fixed horizon bucket, aligned to UTC. bucket.start is floor(t, bucket_duration) and is half of the round identity and of the advisory-lock key. Fixed alignment rather than a rolling window is what makes rounds reproducible and replayable — a rolling window would make the same input produce different partitions depending on when it ran.

trigger.description: CADENCE: the periodic sweep fired. OPPORTUNITY_DEBOUNCE: enough new opportunities landed for this bucket, or the debounce timer expired — this is what makes the demo feel live, since submitting a request visibly ripples into a re-plan. MANUAL: operator-forced, via the admin path. REPLAN: an existing plan for this bucket is being recomputed, which implies supersedes_plan_id is set.

policy.description: The AllocationPolicy this round will run. Carried on the event so that a committed plan can be attributed to a specific strategy after the fact — which is what turns 'which algorithm?' from an argument into a measurement, and what makes the benchmark harness able to replay identical inputs through different policies.

candidate_opportunity_count.description: Opportunities on the table when the round opened. Zero is legal and not an error: a cadence sweep over an empty bucket commits an empty plan, which is a meaningful statement that the satellite is idle.

candidate_request_ids.description: Distinct requests competing in this round. The input side of the ledger: every one of these must appear either as an acquisition in the committed plan or as a planning.request.unfulfilled.v1. A contract test asserts exactly that conservation property, because a request that silently vanishes between rounds is the worst possible failure mode for a customer.

duty_cycle_budget_s.description: Imaging seconds available per orbit for this satellite in this bucket. The knapsack dimension layered on top of the interval constraints.

supersedes_plan_id.description: The plan being replaced, when trigger is REPLAN. Null on a first plan for the bucket.
